title: Mormon’s epistle
summary: Mormon’s letter to Moroni begins with joy at his calling and a prayer for his faithful endurance.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon wrote an epistle to Moroni soon after Moroni’s calling to the ministry.
Mormon rejoiced that the Lord Jesus Christ had called Moroni to his ministry and holy work.
Mormon said he continually prayed for Moroni.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter is shown as a written message; Moroni is its recipient, not necessarily physically present.
unspecified_visual_details: The letter’s material, handwriting, and setting are not stated.

narration.text: An epistle of my father Mormon

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni receiving the letter in person.

title: Disputations over children’s baptism
summary: Mormon tells Moroni that disputes have arisen concerning the baptism of little children and urges him to remove the error.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon said that disputations had arisen among Moroni’s people concerning baptism of little children.
Mormon wrote the epistle so Moroni would labor diligently to remove what Mormon called a gross error.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon is composing or dictating the epistle.
unspecified_visual_details: No other participants in the disputes are identified or described.

narration.text: there should disputations rise among you
concerning the baptism of your little children

prohibited_inventions: Do not show an actual baptism or debate; the passage reports disputes rather than narrating one.

title: The received words of Christ
summary: Moroni reports that after learning of the matter, he inquired of the Lord and received the word of the Lord by the power of the Holy Ghost. The teaching identifies Christ as Redeemer, Lord, and God; explains his call of sinners to repentance using the physician comparison; declares little children whole and incapable of sin; and states that Adam’s curse has no power over them in Christ and that circumcision is done away in him.
characters: Christ (source of the quoted teaching; no visible appearance described)

explicit_facts.text: Moroni reports having inquired of the Lord immediately after learning of the matter.
The word of the Lord came to him by the power of the Holy Ghost.
The teaching introduces the words of Christ, identified as Redeemer, Lord, and God.
Christ states that he came into the world to call sinners, not the righteous, to repentance.
The teaching compares the whole, who need no physician, with the sick, who do.
Little children are whole and incapable of committing sin.
The curse of Adam is taken from little children in Christ and has no power over them.
The law of circumcision is done away in Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A text-focused presentation can distinguish Moroni’s retrospective report from Christ’s quoted teaching without staging either as a newly occurring event.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, surroundings, clothing, and physical posture are unspecified.
The sensory manner of receiving the word is unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I came into the world not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Christ

narration.text: And the word of the Lord came to me by the power of the Holy Ghost, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Retain the inquiry and reception as retrospective reporting rather than a present-tense reenactment.
The introductory instruction to listen is not assigned a separate speaker; the selected first-person teaching is attributed to Christ.
The physician comparison is teaching, not a narrated medical event.
The dialogue is a selected excerpt, not the full extent of the supplied teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible appearance of Christ or the Holy Ghost, or an audible delivery mechanism.
Do not stage Christ’s coming into the world, Adam, children, a physician, or circumcision as events occurring in this scene.
Do not invent the details of the matter learned, an inquiry prayer, or additional dialogue.

title: Mormon’s judgment on infant baptism
summary: Mormon calls baptizing little children a solemn mockery and instructs that repentance and baptism be taught to those accountable and capable of sin.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says baptizing little children is a solemn mockery before God.
Mormon says repentance and baptism should be taught to those accountable and capable of committing sin.
Mormon says little children need neither repentance nor baptism.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon’s instruction is conveyed as writing or off-screen narration, not as a baptism scene.
unspecified_visual_details: No listeners or children are described as present.

narration.text: it is solemn mockery before God
their little children need no repentance, neither baptism.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a baptism or add listeners not stated in the passage.

title: Children alive in Christ
summary: Mormon teaches that little children are alive in Christ and argues against the consequence that unbaptized children would be lost.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says little children are alive in Christ from the foundation of the world.
Mormon asks how many little children have died without baptism and argues that they would otherwise have gone to an endless hell.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The argument can be rendered through Mormon’s letter, without depicting the dead or hell.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular children, deaths, or afterlife appearance are described.

narration.text: little children are alive in Christ
these must have gone to an endless hell.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The consequence in verse 13 is a conditional argument, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray children in hell or invent the circumstances of any child’s death.

title: Warning against the belief
summary: Mormon condemns the belief that children need baptism, warns those who pervert the Lord’s ways to repent, and declares that perfect love casts out fear.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says one who supposes little children need baptism is in bitterness and iniquity and lacks faith, hope, and charity.
Mormon condemns supposing that God saves one child through baptism while another perishes without it.
Mormon says those who pervert the Lord’s ways will perish unless they repent, and says he speaks with authority from God without fear.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon’s forceful address may be shown as lettered narration over his writing.
unspecified_visual_details: No condemned person or divine judgment scene is described.

narration.text: I speak with boldness, having authority from God
perfect love casteth out all fear.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The references to being cut off and going to hell are warnings, not depicted events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray anyone being cut off or sent to hell.

title: Mormon’s love for children
summary: Mormon says he loves little children with perfect love, that they partake of salvation, and that God is unchangeable and merciful to them.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he is filled with everlasting charity and loves little children with perfect love.
Mormon says all children are alike to him and are partakers of salvation.
Mormon says God is not partial or changeable and that little children are alive in him through mercy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon’s teaching may be lettered over his writing; no children need be shown.
unspecified_visual_details: No children are identified or described as physically present.

narration.text: I love little children with a perfect love
they are all alive in him because of his mercy.

prohibited_inventions: Do not visualize salvation or mercy as an unmentioned supernatural event.

title: Mercies of Christ and redemption
summary: Mormon warns that saying little children need baptism denies Christ’s mercies and redemption, and teaches that children and those without the law are alive in Christ.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says the claim that little children need baptism denies Christ’s mercies and the power of his redemption.
Mormon says God commanded him to speak boldly and warns that those who reject the teaching stand against Moroni at Christ’s judgment-seat.
Mormon says little children and those without the law are alive in Christ and that baptism avails nothing for those under no condemnation.
Mormon calls denying Christ’s mercies and trusting in dead works mockery before God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The judgment-seat is mentioned as a future judgment, not shown as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance of Christ or judgment scene is described.

narration.text: all little children are alive in Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The judgment-seat and spiritual consequences are teachings and warnings, not present visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ at a judgment-seat or invent a vision.

title: Repentance and baptism
summary: Mormon explains that repentance is for those under condemnation, followed by baptism, remission of sins, meekness, the visitation of the Holy Ghost, hope, and enduring love.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says repentance is for those under condemnation and under the curse of a broken law.
Mormon describes baptism as the first fruits of repentance and says fulfilling commandments brings remission of sins.
Mormon says remission brings meekness and lowliness of heart, followed by the visitation of the Holy Ghost, hope, perfect love, and diligence in prayer.
Mormon says the saints will dwell with God when the end comes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The sequence is presented as teaching in the letter rather than as a montage of events.
unspecified_visual_details: No baptism, Holy Ghost appearance, or future dwelling place is visually described.

narration.text: the first fruits of repentance is baptism
the visitation of the Holy Ghost

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The described spiritual sequence is doctrinal teaching, not a set of narrated visual events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible Holy Ghost or a specific heavenly setting.

title: Mormon’s concern for the Nephites
summary: Mormon says he may go out against the Lamanites, warns of Nephite pride and rejection of God’s power, asks Moroni to pray for them, and closes the epistle.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he will write again if he does not go out soon against the Lamanites.
Mormon says the pride of the Nephites has proven their destruction unless they repent.
Mormon asks Moroni to pray for the Nephites and fears the Spirit has ceased striving with them; he says they are seeking to put down power and authority from God and denying the Holy Ghost.
Mormon says the Nephites must perish soon after rejecting knowledge, in fulfillment of prophecy.
Mormon bids farewell to Moroni until he writes again or they meet again.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The closing lines may be shown as the end of Mormon’s letter.
unspecified_visual_details: The location of Mormon’s possible campaign and the Lamanites are not depicted or described here.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon’s possible departure and predicted destruction are not narrated as occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict combat, Nephite destruction, or an in-person meeting.
